rv.q: Elektra draws its centrifugal power from the harmony at its core, and the harshly beautiful, straight-tone Balkan belt of these six vocalists pierces as brazenly as Elektra’s own howling in the darkness.
Along with the Chorus—Catherine Brookman, Sophia Rose Byrd, Mingjia Chen, Tina Fabrique, Maya Lagerstam, Tanner Porter—the acting ensemble is uniformly dynamic. This, however, is Benko’s showcase.
Daniel Fish's Elektra, on the other hand, has been drained of all its power.
I just wish that Fish had trusted his material over his desire to turn the stage into a soapbox.

Scenic designers Jim Findlay, Josh Higgason, and Amy C. Rubin have transformed the malleable Polonsky in Brooklyn into a car wash, with a long, narrow runway/platform in the center, with limited seating on three sides of the action. The cast walks across the platform and into the pit surrounding it or sit on folding chairs.

cn.t: Mixed reception: Benko's fierce performance and Hearne's a cappella choral work earn praise, but heavy-handed modernization undercuts Sophocles' timeless tragedy.
